optionReasons.saa-ini-014:option:0: Access keys permanent per employee is the anti-standard: duplicate long-term credentials outside the directory.
optionReasons.saa-ini-014:option:1: Root credentials NUNCA share — is the most critical identity of the account.
optionReasons.saa-ini-014:option:3: Replicate/copy AD users to the IAM double management — the federation avoids exactly that.

finalJustifications: Because the federation integrates the corporate IoP (AD) to AWS: the employee authenticates in the directory and assumes roles with temporary credentials — without users IAM duplicated.
Because the federation migrates AD users to the IAM in a single charge, keeping corporate passwords already known by employees.
Because the federation requires the Active Directory installed in an instance EC2, from where AWS validates each corporate login received.
Because the federation converts AD passwords into key accesses from AWS, delivered to employees for use in CLI and on the console.

optionReasons.saa-ini-015:option:0: The Secrets Manager keep application secrets — not corporate login portal.
optionReasons.saa-ini-015:option:1: The Cognito authentic USERS FINAIS of apps — or SSO of labor force for multiple accounts is the Identity Center.
optionReasons.saa-ini-015:option:3: The ACM issue certificates SSL/TLS — nothing to do with login.

finalJustifications: Because IAM Identity Center (ex-AWS SSO) centralizes the unique workforce login for multiple accounts and applications, with centrally managed permissions.
Because Identity Center replaces the IAM in all Member Accounts, unifying permissions in a single central directory.
Because Identity Center works only with Microsoft's Active Directory, the directory required for the portal of SSO.
Because Identity Center issues an account access certificate, and the portal only organises the 15 certificates in one place.

optionReasons.saa-ini-016:option:0: The IAM DA identity management CONTA AWS (equipment/services) — no end-users of application.
optionReasons.saa-ini-016:option:1: The Identity Center It's SSO FORCE OF TRABALHO — no registration/social login of app customers.
optionReasons.saa-ini-016:option:3: Directory Service hosts Active Directory managed — for Windows corporate environments, not mobile apps.

finalJustifications: Because Cognito (user pools) delivers registration, login with social providers, password recovery and tokens to protect APIs — made for end users of apps.
Because Cognito creates a user IAM for each client of the application, isolating the permissions of each end user account.
Because Cognito store user passwords in S3 with encryption, the durable basis required for password recovery.
Because Cognito is the only service of AWS approved for mobile applications, with SDKs exclusive to iOS and native Android.

optionReasons.saa-ini-034:option:0: It's the elements. FUNCIONAIS policy centres — no comments.
optionReasons.saa-ini-034:option:1: There is no relationship with encryption, time or type of instance in these fields.
optionReasons.saa-ini-034:option:2: Effect is not cost, Action is not user and Resource is not Region.

finalJustifications: Because Effect = Allow/Deny, Action = which operations API (ex.: s3:GetObject) and Resource = to which NRAs the declaration applies — the core of any policy IAM.
Because Effect defines the affected service, Action the method HTTP of the call and Resource to the Region where the policy is applied by default.
Because the three elements are automatically inherited from the user group, and the policy only overwrites them when necessary.
Because Effect and Action become optional when Resource uses asterisk — the curinga already implies total permission to the resource.

optionReasons.saa-ini-035:option:0: High availability is about RESILENCE — not about limiting permissions.
optionReasons.saa-ini-035:option:1: Horizontal scalability is over CAPACIDADE — Nothing to do with the permission drawing..
optionReasons.saa-ini-035:option:3: Shared responsibility divides duties between AWS and customer — does not guide minimum permissions per component.

finalJustifications: Because the least privilege grants only the minimum necessary to each task — limiting the damage of compromised credentials or errors.
Because the lowest privilege prohibits the use of policies managed by AWS, requiring custom policies by component.
Because the lowest privilege requires double approval for each new permission, the change control of the security team.
Because the least privilege applies only to the root user, the only one with enough power to cause damage to the account.

optionReasons.saa-ini-036:option:0: MFA has no relation to support speed.
optionReasons.saa-ini-036:option:2: Any identity with permission creates EC2 — is not exclusive to root.
optionReasons.saa-ini-036:option:3: The account accesses services normally paid without MFA — o MFA is protection, not pre-requirement of collection.

finalJustifications: Because the root has unlimited power that politics IAM non-restriction — commit to deliver the entire account; MFA + use only emergency is the first rule of safety.
Because root is the only identity that the AWS can't monitor the logs, and the MFA compensates for this account audit gap.
Because MFA in the root unlocks the full free level of the account, including the initial credits of new approved projects.
Because without MFA the root loses access to the console after 90 days, and the credentials kept would cease to be valid in the emergency..

optionReasons.saa-ini-163:option:0: Policies by tag control access to RECURSOS marked — do not impose a ceiling on what a created roller can do.
optionReasons.saa-ini-163:option:1: Groups only AGRUPAM users for common policies — do not limit what others create.
optionReasons.saa-ini-163:option:3: SCPs limit CONTAS in the organisation (and do not affect the management account) — the ceiling by ENTIDADE created by others is the permission boundary.

finalJustifications: Because Permission Boundary defines the entity's MAXIMUM of effective permissions: even if the Dev annexes broad policies, real access never exceeds the Boundary.
Because Permission Boundary grants temporary extra permissions by approval, the controlled elevation flow of the IAM.
Because Permission Boundary copies the creator's permissions to the new roll, preventing the dev from granting more than it has.
Because Permission Boundary blocks the creation of new roles in the account, centralizing the provisioning on the platform team.

optionReasons.saa-ini-169:option:0: VPC Peering connects REDES — does not grant permissions IAM between accounts.
optionReasons.saa-ini-169:option:1: Sharing the root is the maximum security breach.
optionReasons.saa-ini-169:option:3: Duplicate users with the same credentials is precisely the anti-standard that the role federation eliminates.

finalJustifications: Because a role in Production with trust policy relying on the Audit account allows sts:AssumeRole: TEMPORARY credentials read only, without duplication.
Because STS synchronizes users between the two accounts automatically, replicating auditors as reading identities.
Because the trust policy converts auditors into native users of Production, with the same passwords as the Audit account.
Because AssumeRole grants permanent access after first use, dispensing new authentications on subsequent visits.
